subject: IP gating, output title, and feedback-license — order form next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karina Soto <karina.soto@novumhealth.com>, Ethan Voss <ethan.voss@novumhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@novumhealth.com
Date: 2026-07-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: IP gating, output title, and feedback-license — order form next steps

Hi Karina / Ethan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I attached the latest order form redline and a short MSA excerpt (Proposed_MSAText_Ben_v3.docx) that attempts to hit three things Novum asked for:

- Clear ownership of customer-provided data and customer-owned outputs for your internal product use.
- A narrow carveout allowing Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry & feedback to improve the service (quality/metrics only).
- A restrictive model-retraining clause requiring explicit written consent for any customer-weighted retraining.

Quick ask: can you flag the items that are an immediate blocker for your legal/procurement team vs. items you want on the final MSA but could be handled post-signature (e.g., logging retention windows)? We want to avoid an 'all-or-nothing' hold-up.

Attachments: Novum_OrderForm_Redline_v2.pdf (redlines inline), Proposed_MSAText_Ben_v3.docx (proposed clause language).

I copied our internal legal/product folks (Laura, Markus, Dylan) to keep them in the loop for any technical/ops constraints.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187

From: Karina Soto <karina.soto@novumhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Ethan Voss <ethan.voss@novumhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@novumhealth.com
Date: 2026-07-12T12:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: IP gating, output title, and feedback-license — order form next steps

Ben —

Thanks for the redlines. High-level concerns from legal: 1) the current "feedback" carve in your draft is still broad — it reads like you can ingest and train on Novum outputs unless we opt-out; 2) we need the order form to say Novum retains title to any output used to power our products (not just copies we store); 3) we need assurances around telemetry/PII and a narrow exception for aggregated metrics only.

Specific asks:
- Replace the training clause so retraining requires written "advance" consent (not just notice).
- Explicitly exclude customer PHI/PII from any telemetry/feed processing without encryption/psuedo-anonymization + attestation.
- Add a short statement in the order form that Novum has exclusive title to Outputs for their products, and Redwood will not claim ownership or use Outputs to create competing models.

We can do a concession on telemetry if you agree to: (a) telemetry is strictly for service quality/uptime/aggregate metric improvements; (b) no per-customer model updates without signed amendment; (c) you define the anonymization approach in the SOW or a tech spec.

We are under a procurement timeline next week, so we need changes tracked and a final round by Thursday EOD PT.

-Karina
Karina Soto
Senior Counsel, Novum Health
karina.soto@novumhealth.com

On Tue, Jul 12, 2026 at 9:18 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (original message attached)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karina Soto <karina.soto@novumhealth.com>, Ethan Voss <ethan.voss@novumhealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T12:35:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: IP gating, output title, and feedback-license — order form next steps

Laura / Markus / Dylan —

Karina pushed back pretty hard on two areas: training consent must be advance/written, and Novum wants exclusive title language around Outputs used inside their product. They are open to a narrower telemetry carveout but want us to commit to anonymization + attestation.

Proposed internal approach (short):
1) Offer two-line compromise language in the MSA: confirm "Customer retains title to Outputs" and "Redwood will not use Outputs to create customer-specific model weights absent a signed amendment."
2) Move the operational details (anonymization approach, retention windows) to a tech spec/SOW that both teams sign — this lets product/ops iterate without MSA re-signs.
3) For the training clause, replace the opt-out style with a clause that allows Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified feedback for model quality work and requires explicit signed consent for retraining involving customer signals.

Draft proposed sentence for Laura to vet (short, legal-ready):
"Except as set forth in a mutually executed amendment, Customer retains ownership of Outputs and Redwood will not use Customer Outputs to train or create Customer-specific model weights without Customer's prior written consent."

Markus — can you confirm the feasibility of the anonymization / attestation approach and whether we can operationalize a standard tech-spec that will satisfy legal? Dylan — any product/ops constraints on splitting telemetry details into a SOW?

If we can present the single-line compromise + SOW approach back to Karina today, we should be able to hit Novum's procurement window.

Thanks —
Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karina Soto <karina.soto@novumhealth.com>, Ethan Voss <ethan.voss@novumhealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: IP gating, output title, and feedback-license — order form next steps

Ben / team —

Thanks — I reviewed Ben's proposed language and marked up the attached doc with a slightly tighter clause and fallback language for telemetry. High-level: I agree with the single-line ownership confirmation in the MSA and moving operational details to a SOW. I tightened "aggregated, de-identified" to reference a minimal de-identification standard and added a binding requirement for Redwood to provide a periodic attestation (quarterly) that data processed for quality was not reversible to customer-identities.

Suggested clause (one line for MSA):
"Customer retains title to Outputs; Redwood will not use Customer Outputs to train or create Customer-specific model weights without Customer's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld."

Fallback telemetry language (SOW/tech spec):
- "Telemetry shall be collected and processed only after pseudonymization such that individual customer identities cannot be reasonably re-identified; Redwood will provide quarterly attestations and may only use aggregated metrics for model-quality improvements unless an explicit amendment is executed."

Markus confirmed offline that we can ship a standard tech-spec for anonymization and provide the quarterly attestation. Dylan indicated no product blockers for moving details to an SOW.

Ben — please send the updated redline back to Karina with these two inserts and emphasize we can execute the attestation + SOW flow to avoid repeated MSA redlines. If procurement pushes on credits for restrictions, flag to me and I'll escalate a one-time onboarding credit.

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: Novum_OrderForm_Redline_v2.pdf (updated with MSA one-liner), Proposed_MSAText_Ben_v3.docx (redline with Laura's comments)
